revision_history.note: initial prospective draft by the Slice 2C preparation owner: composition objective, plane identity, composition refusals, selection checks, A/B/C comparisons with the prospective A-vs-B relation, copy accounting, mutation controls, frozen synthetic population. No composition code exists and nothing was observed.

folds in the planner's resolutions of the draft-1 open questions (2026-09-24), requirements only: child independence from R1 and the production decoder at source and symbol level (C7); a required public-interface test for the sealed plane (I-PLANE-SINGLE-INDEX); the Slice 2B regression requirement stated exactly (unchanged test set, byte-identical 363-case report e3b596bc..., unchanged gate counts), with the recorded finding that report byte-identity is unattainable as stated (slice2c-plan.md section 6.2), open for the planner; the composition CI step REQUIRED through doctor X/Y with mutation controls (C10). No relation, refusal predicate, selection check, comparison, assumption or fixture changed; generator, manifest and fixtures byte-unchanged. The manifest's contract_schema field keeps naming draft.1, the draft under which the population was generated.

prospective_statement: Every relation, refusal, check and acceptance criterion in this file was written before any composition code existed and before any Slice 2C observation. No MLX operation, native bridge call, qualification child, composition path or Rust R1 was run while drafting it. The fixture population was produced by a stdlib-only generator whose only arithmetic is exact integer offset/size arithmetic and the frozen Slice 2B domain classifier; the generator's oracle does not call production slicing (mlx_affine::AffineTriple::expert_slice / row_slice) or the production decoder. One non-numerical sanity observation preceded this file and is disclosed: the committed fixture checkpoints were opened with the Slice 1 catalog (Checkpoint::open, QuantizationConfig::from_config_json, validate_catalog, classify_module) in a throwaway program that was not committed; it confirmed admission and the resolved (bits, group) of every module, that ck-a-single and ck-a-sibling have the same catalog digest, and that dropping the block.1.stack_d override is refused as InconsistentOverride with implied_bits 8. No range, byte or number from any selection or execution was observed.

correction_policy.rule_1: An observation that exceeds a bound, violates an exact invariant, or fails any acceptance criterion is a FAIL. It is recorded against the original criteria of the contract version under which it was observed and is retained permanently.
correction_policy.rule_2: Any revision of a relation, a refusal, an assumption, a check or an acceptance criterion is a new, separately identified contract version (new schema version string and file hash) that must be independently reviewed and explicitly authorized by the owner before any renewed qualification run.
correction_policy.rule_3: No appended entry, correction, erratum or replacement contract may convert a recorded failure into a pass, and no threshold is moved in place. A renewed qualification under a revised contract is a new run with its own evidence; the earlier failure remains a failure of the earlier version.
correction_policy.rule_4: The qualification report binds the sha256 of this contract file, the fixture manifest, the generator and the Slice 2B contract; a report produced under a different contract version cannot satisfy this version's acceptance criteria.
correction_policy.failure_triage: Every failed attempt is preserved with candidate commit and contract identity. An implementation defect gets a targeted fix and a separately identified rerun. A contract defect, a scope expansion, an unsupported prerequisite or a numerical-rule change is a STOP reported to the planner.

invariants.statement: A SelectedPlane has exactly one index_path and exactly one source/module binding; its three ranges are derived inside one constructor from one resolved triple and that one index path. It has no public field, no setter, no constructor or builder that accepts per-component ranges, tensors or indices, and no way to replace one component of an existing plane. Weight from expert A cannot be combined with scales or biases from expert B, or from another module or source, through any public API.
invariants.verification: REQUIRED public-interface test (slice2c-plan.md section 2.2): (1) an API audit of the plane module's source: no pub or pub(crate) field, no Default or Clone, the only public functions returning a SelectedPlane are select_plane and compose (one index path and one triple or module each), no public function taking a ByteSlice, TripleSlice, raw range or component bytes, and no &mut self method; (2) every public entry (E-COMPOSE, E-SELECT) driven with cross-module and cross-source components must refuse (C-R-MODULE-BINDING, C-R-SOURCE-BINDING), and every accepted plane's three ranges must be those of the one requested index. Mutation controls mut-swap-scales and mut-swap-biases, injected at the selection-record level through the test-only child path, show that a mixed selection, if it ever arose, is detected by S-RANGES and S-BYTES before native execution

invariants.statement: the plane borrows its three byte ranges from the immutable backing (lifetime tied to the backing); it does not own copies; the backing is never mutated while any plane borrows it

no complete float32 (or any float) weight matrix of the plane is created on the QMM path; the packed U32 words are staged and imported unchanged (inherits native-primitives-v1.json#scope.packed_weight_path)
no unsafe reinterpretation (pointer casts, transmute, align_to, from_raw_parts) is used to avoid a copy; the library crate remains #![forbid(unsafe_code)]

composition_refusals.principle: Checked in this order, on host data, before any MLX-C call of the case (no import, no numerical call); the first failing check's id is returned as a typed error and the case records it. The inherited Slice 2B refusals then apply to the selected plane, in their frozen order, inside the existing bridge, also before any MLX-C numerical call or import.

order.condition: Slice 1 catalog admission fails (any catalog-contract.md refusal); the Slice 1 variant is recorded. No Slice 2C probe: the Slice 1 negative corpus already covers these and is not duplicated.

classify_module does not return Quantized for the module under the configuration (unknown module, incomplete triple, override inconsistent with the stored shapes, scales without configuration, ...); the Slice 1 AffineError variant and, for InconsistentOverride, implied_bits are recorded
the backing's source identity (shard file names and sha256 values, recorded when the backing was loaded) differs from the opened checkpoint's (Checkpoint::hash_shards provenance)

the triple's weight, scales or biases TensorMeta is not the checkpoint catalog's authoritative entry for <module>.weight, <module>.scales, <module>.biases respectively (name and full TensorMeta equality)
index_path length != the triple's number of leading dimensions
rank matches and some index >= its leading extent (including values near u64::MAX, which are never wrapped, truncated or narrowed)

a checked u64/usize operation of the composition layer's range arithmetic overflows (begin + len, begin or end conversion). Through an admitted catalog and a validated AffineTriple this is unreachable (catalog rules 10-12 and 24b; Slice 1 C-SLICE); the probe exercises E-RANGE directly
a selected range's end exceeds the length of the backing (window) of its shard, or the checkpoint has no backing (header-only)

composition_refusals.evaluation_rule: The generator evaluates every composition guard from C-R-RESOLVE on independently (manifest composition_refusal_order and oracle.composition_guards; C-R-CATALOG is omitted there because it has no Slice 2C probe and every fixture checkpoint is admissible); a guard whose precondition fails is recorded as not evaluable. Every FX-COMP-REFUSE probe violates EXACTLY ONE evaluable guard, its expected id; every accepted and inherited-refusal case violates none.
composition_refusals.instrumentation: The child samples the existing MLX-C call counters (numerical, imports; crates/mlx-native-affine/src/bin/qualify/ffi.rs call_counts) at case start and at the refusal decision and records both deltas; for a composition refusal or a detected mutation the whole-case delta must be (0, 0). For inherited refusals the existing OpStats numerical_before_decision and imports_before_decision must be 0. The parent enforces both from the report.

selection_checks.principle: Exact comparisons of the candidate's selection against the manifest oracle, performed in the child before any native call (so a wrong plane is never executed) and re-decided by the parent from the reported values (the parent never trusts a child verdict).

checks.statement: every plane_identity field except ranges equals oracle.identity exactly
for each component: (shard file name, absolute begin, length) equals oracle.ranges exactly
for each component: sha256 of the borrowed bytes equals oracle.sha256 (the sha256 of the oracle's expected plane bytes, which are also the standalone file's w/scales/biases tensors)
A's staged HostTensors w, scales, biases and x are byte-identical, with identical dtype and shape, to B's HostTensors loaded from the standalone file
the sha256 of every shard file and of every backing buffer after extraction and after native execution equals the manifest's file sha256 recorded before; the standalone file is re-hashed after B

selection_checks.oracle_independence: oracle.ranges and oracle.sha256 are computed by the generator from the fixture specification (tensor placement chosen by its writer plus index * plane_bytes from (N, K, bits, group, dtype)) and cross-checked against a separate stdlib parse of the written headers and against slices of the written files; the test re-derives the ranges with its own header reader. None of them calls the Slice 1 slicing or decoding code.

comparisons.B: the standalone plane: the oracle's expected w/scales/biases and x loaded from standalone/<id>.bin with the Slice 2B fixture loader, through the SAME bridge quantized_matmul, in the same child, on the same NativeContext and GPU stream, with the same bits, group size and transpose, immediately after A

the float32 output bytes of A and B are identical, bit for bit, including the sign of zero, for every element
within one child, seq-aba-2's A output bytes equal seq-aba-0's A output bytes bit for bit (same selection, same x), with seq-aba-1 (another module at another bit width) executed between them

the arrays the composed path creates are exactly the manifest's array_census: imports x F32 [M,K], w U32 [N,K*bits/32], scales and biases BF16 [N,K/group]; astype scales_f32 and biases_f32 F32 [N,K/group]; output F32 [M,N]; no other array, and in particular no float array of the weight's logical shape

a_vs_b_relation.relation: EXACT BITWISE EQUALITY (N-COMP-AB). No tolerance is defined and none may be substituted.
premises: Identical inputs: S-STAGED-EQUAL establishes byte-identical x, w, scales, biases with identical dtypes and shapes before either execution.

Identical operation and settings: both go through the one existing bridge entry (quantized_matmul, transpose=true, same bits, group size, OP-CAST on the same explicit GPU stream of the same NativeContext, default device GPU), in the same child process, adjacent in time, with MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 (A-NONAX).

Identical kernel: QuantizedMatmul::eval_gpu chooses the kernel only from transpose, M, N, K, the batch count, bits, group size, x dtype and the device (MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp:1386-1454; get_qmv_batch_limit depends on K, N and the device); qmm_splitk's split_k depends only on M, N, K and group size (quantized.cpp:787-803). Every input is made row-contiguous by the same rule (ensure_row_contiguous_matrix, quantized.cpp:1393-1400), and mlx_array_new_data imports are already row-contiguous, so no conditional copy distinguishes A from B.

No order-dependent accumulation visible in source: there is no atomic operation in MLX312:mlx/backend/metal/kernels/quantized.h or mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp; the split-K partial sums are written to an intermediate array (quantized.cpp:818-820) by distinct threadgroups and reduced by strided_reduce_general_dispatch (quantized.cpp:860-866), whose column-reduce kernels write each output non-atomically (mlx/backend/metal/kernels/reduction/reduce_col.h:86-90, 139, 250-254, 283-287, 390-394; that file contains no atomic operation). The only floating-point atomic add, Sum::atomic_update (kernels/reduction/ops.h:130-131), is reached from the scatter kernels (kernels/indexing/scatter.h:57, scatter_axis.h:51), not from this path.

Under D-GEOM every element of the split-K intermediate and of the output is written before it is read (N % 64 == 0 alignment, native-primitives-v1.json#domains.D-GEOM.justification.N_mod_64), so uninitialised allocator memory cannot reach a result.
a_vs_b_relation.failure_policy: A single differing bit in any element is a FAIL of N-COMP-AB, recorded for that case and contract version and never reclassified. Triage, without retry: if S-STAGED-EQUAL or S-BYTES failed, it is an implementation defect (targeted fix, separately identified rerun). If every input check passed and A and B still differ, A-DET is falsified for this build and host: STOP and report to the planner; replacing bitwise equality by any tolerance or by the R1 gates alone is a new contract version (correction_policy.rule_2). A and B must each still pass the inherited R1 gates against C; passing those never excuses an N-COMP-AB failure.

A-DET.statement: On one device, in one process, the same compiled Metal pipeline dispatched with the same grid and threadgroup geometry on byte-identical, identically shaped and identically strided input buffers produces byte-identical outputs. In particular simd_sum, quad_sum (MLX312:quantized.h:742, 809, 913, 969) and simdgroup_multiply_accumulate (A-MMA) evaluate in an order that, although unknown (U4, U5), is fixed for a given pipeline and input, and results do not depend on buffer addresses or on threadgroup scheduling order.
A-DET.basis: Not provable from pinned source: the order of the hardware reductions is not specified (native-primitives-v1.json U4, U5). The source-visible sources of run-to-run variation (atomics, kernel choice, conditional copies, uninitialised reads) are excluded by the premises of comparisons.a_vs_b_relation.
A-DET.if_false: N-COMP-AB fails; the failure policy applies. The inherited bounds are unaffected (they are order-independent).

copy_and_ownership.accounting_method: For every executed case the child reports, per stage P0-P7, each host buffer it allocates or copies (role, dtype, shape, bytes) and each MLX array it creates (role, operation, dtype, shape), taken from the existing import/astype/QMM entry points and the staging code; the parent compares them with the manifest's array_census (N-COMP-ARRAYS) and with the component plane_bytes. Borrowed ranges are reported as borrows (begin, length, backing shard), not as copies.

stages.fixture_load: one immutable host buffer per shard (a prefix window when the manifest declares one); the only copy of source bytes before staging
stages.host_selection: borrowed &[u8] sub-slices of the backing; zero copies
stages.staging: one copy of exactly plane_bytes[component] into each Slice 2B HostTensor (the bridge API takes owned HostTensors; changing that API is not authorized)
stages.metadata_widening: OP-CAST creates two float32 arrays of the metadata shape [N, K/group] only
stages.execution: one float32 output [M, N]; the packed U32 weight is consumed unchanged; the kernels decode codes transiently (native-primitives-v1.json#scope.packed_weight_path)
stages.readback: one host copy of the output through the Evaluated typestate (E2)

copy_and_ownership.lifetimes: backing outlives every plane that borrows it; HostTensors are owned by the case; NativeArray<'ctx> handles are dropped before the case ends (zero live arrays between cases, as in Slice 2B)
prohibited: a complete float weight matrix on the QMM path
mutation of the backing while borrowed

mutation_controls.principle: A mutation control proves that the independent checks are SENSITIVE to one specific selection defect. The harness injects the defect at the selection-record level through a test-only path of the child (never through a public plane constructor): it replaces the named ranges or identity fields of the record, reads the bytes at the mutated ranges from the backing, and submits the mutated record to the same checks. Every listed check must report a mismatch, the mutation must have taken effect exactly as the manifest specifies (the mutated ranges and sha256 equal composition.mutation.ranges/sha256), and no native call is issued in the case. A control that is not detected, or detected by a different set of checks, is a FAIL.

controls.defect: selection arithmetic uses expert (e+1) mod E while the identity records e
weight plane stride one u32 word too large on expert 2 of 4 (stays inside the tensor; invisible on expert 0 by construction)
scales of expert 2 with weight and biases of expert 3
biases of expert 0 with weight and scales of expert 1 (three shards)
the 8-bit override is dropped from the configuration
the plane records the 4-bit default for an 8-bit-override module (ranges and bytes unchanged)

mutation_controls.detectability_precondition: Every expert of every module has pairwise-distinct packed weights, scales and biases (asserted by the generator and the test), so a range defect that selects another expert's component changes that component's bytes.
mutation_controls.not_claimed: Arbitrary corrupted bytes are NOT claimed detectable without an identity or reference check: a byte change inside a correctly selected range is detected only by S-BYTES against the oracle hash (fixtures) or by the R1 gates, and in production (no oracle) only by a payload identity such as a verified shard sha256. Mutations are not claimed to cover every possible selection defect.

frozen_population.files_listing_method: inside fixtures/native-composition: find checkpoints mutations standalone -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs shasum -a 256 | shasum -a 256 (27 files: 9 checkpoint files (5 shards, 1 index, 3 configs), 1 mutated config, 17 standalone case files; the manifest records the same value)

composition.FX-COMP-ACCEPT: 11: first/middle/last experts; vector and matrix x; 4-bit default and 8-bit override; single shard and three shards; companions in three different shards; a tensor starting at data offset 0; K 128/256/512 covering qmv_quad, qmv, qmv_fast and qmm_t_splitk (split_k 2, 4, 8); the admitted expert of a module with a refused expert
composition.FX-COMP-SEQUENCE: 3: A-B-A in one child (8-bit expert 1, 4-bit default module, 8-bit expert 1 again with the same x)
composition.FX-COMP-REFUSE: 8: C-R-INDEX-RANGE x2 (E, 2^64-1), C-R-INDEX-RANK x2 ([], [0,0]), C-R-OVERFLOW (E-RANGE probe), C-R-BACKING (window one byte short), C-R-SOURCE-BINDING (identical-header sibling), C-R-MODULE-BINDING (stack_a weight with stack_b companions through AffineTriple::new)

frozen_population.prng: Slice 2B splitmix64 and value draws (draw_codes, draw_meta, draw_x, draw_float) loaded read-only from the sha256-verified Slice 2B generator; per-draw seed = first 8 bytes (big-endian) of sha256(b'f020-2c:' + label)
frozen_population.regeneration: `--check` regenerates every file in memory and requires byte equality and no extra file; the test regenerates twice into fresh directories and compares with the committed tree
frozen_population.parent_validation: Before accepting a child report the parent verifies: (1) sha256(manifest.json) == manifest_sha256 above; (2) every checkpoint file's and standalone file's sha256 == the manifest's; (3) the files listing sha256 == files_listing_sha256; (4) the report's case-id set equals the manifest's exactly (no missing, unexpected or duplicate id); (5) the report echoes this contract's, the manifest's, the generator's and the Slice 2B contract's sha256; any mismatch is a FAIL

execution.child: a new mode of the existing qualify child (e.g. --mode compose), not a change to --mode qualify; the same start-environment assertion (R-NAX), single error handler, default device GPU, provenance (E3), E4 canary at start and end, one NativeContext, one thread, all cases in manifest order (the three seq-aba cases consecutive), report written atomically
execution.parent: a separate parent test target that launches the compose child with the Slice 2B fixed environment and the frozen CHILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS watchdog (SIGKILL, waitpid, TIMEOUT, no retry); the parent failure conditions of native-primitives-v1.json#error_handling.child_process apply unchanged; cleanup accounting (cleanup.errors empty, result handles balanced, zero live arrays at context drop, no double free) as in Slice 2B
execution.slice_2b_regression: REQUIRED of every Slice 2C candidate, on the GitHub macos-15 runner of job apple-mlx-small-fixtures: (1) the Slice 2B step's test set is unchanged: `cargo test -p mlx-native-affine --release -- --list` and `--doc -- --list` are identical at base 12b06367 and at the candidate; (2) the 363-case Slice 2B child report is byte-identical to the attempt-3 report, sha256 e3b596bc6d3c3af3eca33d8084c1a9cb3b0c6bbd2b8910d3bbe7c4e32cac5640 (docs/architecture/reviews/evidence/f020-slice2b-ci-qualification-attempt-3-v1.json, run 36006063937); (3) the Slice 2B gate counts equal attempt 3's exactly, all passed, with 363 cases and no failure. Recorded finding: (2) is unattainable as stated, because the report embeds the qualify executable's sha256, the rustc version, runner-built native-library hashes and allocator observations (slice2c-plan.md section 6.2). A mismatch is a STOP reported to the planner, and no weaker comparison may be substituted without a planner decision.

reporting_and_ci.report: the child report carries schema pulsarmlx.f020.slice2c-child-report/1.0.0, echoes contract_sha256, manifest_sha256, generator_sha256 and slice2b_contract_sha256, and per case: id, outcome (executed | refused | detected | error), refusal id or detected checks, call-counter deltas, selection record (identity, ranges, sha256), copy/array census, A and B output files with sha256 (executed cases)
reporting_and_ci.summary: the parent summary (schema pulsarmlx.f020.slice2c-qualification/1.0.0) records exact case-id accounting (31 ids), per-gate case counts, every failure, the frozen hashes, the child outcome and timeout, and the host architecture
reporting_and_ci.ci: a new REQUIRED step in the native small-fixture job apple-mlx-small-fixtures, after the Slice 2B step, running only the composition parent target (owner GO).
